children: is recalling about 202,000 Jeep vehicles in the US after a software problem was found that could interfere with the vehicles’ tire-pressure monitoring systems.

The recall affects 201,976 vehicles, including selected Jeep Wagoneer, Grand Cherokee, Grand Wagoneer,Wagoneer and Cherokee models, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Certain long-wheelbase and plug-in hybrid versions are also covered.

The software defect could stop the system from recognizing insufficient tire pressure or from displaying the appropriate warning to the driver. That could increase the possibility of a crash because drivers may not be alerted to a potentially unsafe tire condition, NHTSA said.
The regulator also determined that the affected vehicles don't meet US federal requirements for tire-pressure monitoring systems.
will address the problem by having dealers install an updated version of the radio-frequency hub software. The repair will be provided to vehicle owners without charge.
The recall involves vehicles sold in the US. NHTSA's announcement did not cite any crashes or injuries linked to the defect.

title: Stellantis pulls 202,000 Jeeps from US roads over safety software bug
